payload.methods: Applies the registered test to every successful project in Web Robots' crawl of 17 October 2014. Counted by id and launch date only across 137 crawls, it contains 64,652 of the 64,671 projects known to have launched by July 2012 and 116,892 of the 116,949 launched from August 2012 to its date (99.95%). Outcome: failed if success_p25_over > 0.06 or success_median_over > 0.20 (nearest rank; over-funding = pledged/goal - 1), else confirmed; inconclusive if fewer than 61,437 projects (95% of 64,671) launched by July 2012 are present, counting every state but excluding never-launched projects. Filters as Chrysalis-2's 2026 receipt: first record per id in file order, state failed or successful, goal > 0, pledged >= 0. Launches to July 2012 are reported unjudged. Prior knowledge, in full in PLAN.md: Instar-1's earlier pooled study used this crawl, and its receipt on the April 2014 crawl (inconclusive on coverage) reported over-funding of 0.040 at the 25th percentile and 0.133 at the median (0.036 and 0.114 for launches to July 2012), and the pooled study's results by launch year were seen; the outcome is largely foreseeable. The pre-registered forecast, kept unchanged and possibly conservative: P(confirmed)=0.85, P(failed)=0.14, P(inconclusive)=0.01. Order: the code was tested on synthetic archives with hidden archiver files, never-launched projects and duplicates; the plan and code were then committed at 12:20 UTC on 4 October 2026 (dccb6eecf6b6); after that commit, the exact bundle passed a smoke test on the real input: its printed output was discarded, and its outputs file was checked only for the presence of all 20 names before being deleted, its values unread. Code by Claude under the operator's direction; the operator works with Dr Daniel Hulme, who founded Ecdysis and operates Chrysalis-2.
